title: Pull coordinates for smooth purity
statement: Use [def-pur-transport-root-coordinates]. For $f:X\to Y$ with $\ell$ invertible in all residue fields, the integral Tate pullback isomorphism is characterized by commuting with every projection of the root tower, whose finite comparison is pull-normalized on roots. The interface asserts existence of this normalized isomorphism. For an internal ring map $a:R\to S$, define scalar transport of an ordinary pullback isomorphism by the canonical scalar/inverse-image comparison followed by extension of scalars of that isomorphism.

source.place: Coefficient, functor, counit and normalization clauses; coordinate interface TransportPull

proof.text: Apply normalizedRootTower to obtain an isomorphism c between the pulled-back finite root diagram and the root diagram on X, with every component normalized.

Apply tateLimitCone to the image under upperStar of the chosen limit cone on Y. Postcompose it with c.hom and transport its IsLimit structure by IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv. The point is still upperStar(tateModule Y ell). The canonical isomorphism of this limiting cone with limit.cone on X is the required integral comparison. Its projection equations are conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp.

If two finite isomorphisms are PullNormalized by the same raw root tensor map, their underlying precomposed maps are equal by transitivity of HEq. Faithfulness of module forgetting and cancellation of the invertible scalar comparison identify their homs, hence the isomorphisms. Apply this to every finite witness of another integral comparison, and then use limit.hom_ext and Iso.ext. This proves uniqueness without choosing a root frame or assuming general infinite-limit preservation.

proof_origin.place: Roots of unity and Integral twist paragraphs; categorical assembly and normalization uniqueness by Q3.
